title: decode.rs: base64 pre-truncation rounded to multiple-of-4 is correct
description: decode.rs lines 57-58: max_b64_chars = n.saturating_mul(4).div_ceil(3).next_multiple_of(4). This correctly handles the constraint that the STANDARD (padded) base64 engine rejects inputs whose length is not a multiple of 4. A future contributor might suggest removing next_multiple_of(4) as 'redundant' because div_ceil(3) looks close. It is not redundant: 4*ceil(n/3) is not always a multiple of 4 (e.g. n=5 gives ceil(20/3)=7, which is not divisible by 4). The extra next_multiple_of(4) is load-bearing and the test_base64_max_bytes_non_multiple_of_4 test validates it. Do not remove.
close_reason: Confirmed: decode.rs line 58 applies .next_multiple_of(4) to the computed max_b64_chars bound. This is load-bearing: the STANDARD (padded) base64 engine rejects inputs whose length is not a multiple of 4. Rounding up prevents spurious decode errors when pre-truncating to a preview size. Test test_base64_max_bytes_non_multiple_of_4 exercises this for all max_bytes in 1..=10.
